\section[saudável]{saudável — healthy}

\label{lesson:PT-C490-saudavel}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for shiver, then the Portuguese for cramp.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: saudável}
\textbf{saudável} — \textquotedblleft{}healthy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Tento comer de forma saudável.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I try to eat in a healthy way.}
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{saudáveis}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{saudável} is built on \emph{saúde} \textquotedblleft{}health\textquotedblright{}, which is inherited from Latin \emph{salūs} \textquotedblleft{}health, safety\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saudável}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saudável}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{saudável}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for shiver, then the Portuguese for cramp, then say \emph{saudável} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does saudável mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Healthy\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[sedentário]{sedentário — sedentary}

\label{lesson:PT-C490-sedentario}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for cramp, then the Portuguese for healthy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: sedentário}
\textbf{sedentário} — \textquotedblleft{}sedentary\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Com o trabalho no escritório, levo uma vida sedentária.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{With my office job, I lead a sedentary life.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Uma vida sedentária} — a life with little exercise.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sedentário} comes from Latin \emph{sedentārius} \textquotedblleft{}sitting, sedentary\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built on \emph{sedēre} \textquotedblleft{}to sit\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[alongar]{alongar — to stretch; to lengthen}

\label{lesson:PT-C490-alongar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for healthy, then the Portuguese for sedentary.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: alongar}
\textbf{alongar} — \textquotedblleft{}to stretch; to lengthen\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Depois de correr, alongo as pernas.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{After running, I stretch my legs.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Fazer alongamentos} — to do stretches.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{alongar} is built from \emph{a-} and \emph{longo} \textquotedblleft{}long\textquotedblright{}, which is inherited from Latin \emph{longus} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[suar]{suar — to sweat}

\label{lesson:PT-C490-suar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for sedentary, then the Portuguese for to stretch.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: suar}
\textbf{suar} — \textquotedblleft{}to sweat\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
No ginásio suo muito.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I sweat a lot at the gym.}
\end{quote}

Sweat is \emph{o suor}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{suar} is inherited, through Old Portuguese, from Latin \emph{sūdāre} \textquotedblleft{}to sweat\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[a massagem]{a massagem — massage}

\label{lesson:PT-C490-massagem}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to stretch, then the Portuguese for to sweat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a massagem}
\textbf{a massagem} — \textquotedblleft{}massage\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Depois do jogo, o jogador fez uma massagem às costas.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{After the match, the player had a back massage.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Fazer uma massagem} — to give or have a massage.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{massagem} is usually traced to French \emph{massage}, built on \emph{masser} \textquotedblleft{}to knead\textquotedblright{}; the source of the French verb is usually traced to Arabic, but it is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a massagem}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a massagem}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a massagem}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to stretch, then the Portuguese for to sweat, then say \emph{a massagem} again

  \item symptom, (medical) tests, diagnosis, to prescribe, treatment

  \item insomnia, to snore, to yawn, shiver, cramp

To sneeze? (\textbf{espirrar}.) Sneeze? (\textbf{o espirro}.) Allergic? (\textbf{alérgico}.) Itch? (\textbf{a comichão}.) To scratch an itch? (\textbf{coçar}.) Migraine? (\textbf{a enxaqueca}.) (\textbf{a entorse}.) Bandage? (\textbf{a ligadura}.) Symptom? (\textbf{o sintoma}.) (medical) tests? (\textbf{as análises}.) Diagnosis? (\textbf{o diagnóstico}.) To prescribe? (\textbf{receitar}.) Treatment? (\textbf{o tratamento}.) Rest? (\textbf{o repouso}.) To cure? (\textbf{curar}.) Cure? (\textbf{a cura}.) To recover? (\textbf{recuperar}.) Recovery? (\textbf{a recuperação}.) Insomnia? (\textbf{a insónia}.) To snore? (\textbf{ressonar}.) To yawn? (\textbf{bocejar}.) Shiver? (\textbf{o arrepio}.) Cramp? (\textbf{a cãibra}.) Healthy? (\textbf{saudável}.) Sedentary?
